B_access_pricing.mcp_access_cost_details: Official setup guides say MCP integration requires a paid plan and usage is billed against the account's normal credits. Another official product page says users can start for free, creating a documentation conflict.
B_access_pricing.linked_software_cost: Official search result reports limited free tier; Starter $20/seat/month, Business $100/seat/month, Enterprise custom. An official article describes $20 and $100 monthly standard prices after June 30, 2026.
B_access_pricing.pricing_model_details: Credits scale with request complexity. Paid plans can opt into on-demand pay-as-you-go usage beyond monthly credits; the article says a fixed per-credit rate applies but does not state the rate. Workspace budget limits and alert thresholds are described.
B_access_pricing.other_access_restrictions: A paid plan is documented as required by setup guides. OAuth is default for named clients; an API key is documented for custom or headless clients. No product-specific OAuth scopes or rate limits are published in the reviewed evidence.
B_access_pricing.restrictions_controlled_by: Vendor for plan and credit eligibility; user or workspace billing administrator for plan choice and on-demand settings. Exact access control enforcement is not documented.

C_capabilities.description_what_how: The endpoint responds to unauthenticated POST with HTTP 401 and a JSON-RPC authentication error. Third-party listings identify tool names, but no public product-server tools/list response was available. The Scalekit connector documents 47 routed tools; Claude's connector listing names three.
C_capabilities.post_interaction_context_structure: Unauthenticated request returns JSON-RPC error object with code -32000, message "Missing or invalid Authorization header. Please authenticate.", and id null. Authenticated tool-result structures were not publicly retrieved.
C_capabilities.authorization_mechanism: The supplied protected-resource metadata advertises authorization server https://oauth.magicpatterns.com, scopes_supported ["openid","email","profile","offline_access"], bearer_methods_supported ["header"]. The supplied authorization-server metadata advertises DCR at https://oauth.magicpatterns.com/oauth2/register, authorization-code, refresh-token, and device-code grants, PKCE S256, token endpoint authentication methods none/client_secret_post/client_secret_basic, and scopes ["email","offline_access","openid","profile"]. The supplied OIDC configuration additionally lists client_credentials. The vendor documents API-key authentication as an alternative, skipped in place of OAuth when a key is present. Token lifetime and revocation were not found.

D_server_side_logic.additional_logic: 1. Third-party Scalekit listing classifies its 47 routed tools as 14 read-only, 26 write, and 7 destructive; it does not establish server annotations on the input endpoint. Claude lists get_design, read_files, update_design without annotations. 2. No MCP-enforced confirmation flow found; the published catalog descriptions include recommendations but their enforcement is unknown. 3. OAuth metadata exposes only openid, email, profile, offline_access; vendor documents API-key alternative and paid-plan requirement. Product-role inheritance, admin switches, allowlists, token lifetime and revocation are Unknown. 4. Vendor setup documents one remote endpoint; no read-only mode, filters, sandbox, or regional variants found. 5. No MCP-specific PII masking or data-scope rules found. 6. MCP calls consume normal account credits; the vendor says usage scales by complexity. No per-call rate limits or result truncation found. 7. Public hosted implementation is unavailable; parameter validation and argument correction are Unknown. 8. MCP-specific logs, audit trails, telemetry and opt-out are Unknown. 9. No feedback/rating tool appears in the identified product tool listings. The separate documentation MCP includes submit_feedback, but is not this product endpoint. 10. Vendor-distributed plugins provide external skills; the product tool descriptions in the Scalekit catalog contain agent instructions, not verifiable server initialize instructions. 11. Whether prior agent actions affect later tools or results is Unknown. 12. The supplied endpoint is one hosted product endpoint; the vendor's documentation-site search MCP is a separate server. 13. Scalekit lists bash, grep, and verify among its routed tools; bash is described as shell-like file operations within a Magic OS. These are third-party listings; their exact scope and restrictions on the input endpoint are unverified.

D_server_side_logic.server_structure_explanation: The vendor's docs also expose a separate documentation-search MCP server, distinct from the product endpoint. Scalekit documents a 47-tool integration for the product, while other catalogues expose three names or no tool list; this suggests differing catalog surfaces or versions, not a verified endpoint-side dynamic tool hierarchy.

E_aggregated.action_count_comment: No official product tool-name reference was found on the vendor site or in its public plugin repository. The official site describes MCP capabilities but gives no exact tool names. The Claude connector directory lists 3 names; Manufact also reports 3. Scalekit reports 47 routed tools; its native-looking names are included after removing the `magicpatternsmcp_` proxy prefix, all marked third-party and unknown default status. The 47-item Scalekit set and three Claude-directory names are listed in actions.json; they may represent different catalog snapshots or naming surfaces. MCP.so has no tool list.

E_aggregated.token_method: The hosted endpoint's tool definitions and initialize instructions were not available verbatim; no equivalent public server implementation exists in the repository.
E_aggregated.human_can_agent_cannot: Humans can generate interfaces, import design systems from Figma or Storybook, link GitHub repositories, edit prototypes visually, and use Magic Patterns' web application. MCP is documented for accessing designs and design systems and moving layouts between code and the product, but exact MCP coverage and unsupported human operations are not enumerated. Sources: https://www.magicpatterns.com/product/mcp; https://www.magicpatterns.com/blog/aeo/blog/implementation-guide/set-up-the-magic-patterns-mcp-server-connect-your-coding-agent-to-your-design

F_documentation.implementation_hints_not_enforced: The setup guide says to add an Integration Skill: “It tells your agent to treat each design as a spec and adapt it to your codebase's components and conventions, rather than pasting the prototype verbatim.” This is client-side guidance; enforcement by the server is not shown. It also recommends pasting a specific design URL to trigger lookup.
F_documentation.governance_promises: The vendor says MCP calls use the account's normal credits and describes design-system context as the source for generated output. No MCP-specific statements about data retention, AI training, masking, tool-call logging, or permission inheritance were found. The Trust Center page describes security posture but exposed no detailed policy text in the collected copy.
F_documentation.promises_to_user: The vendor says the remote server connects coding agents to designs and design systems, supports a code-to-design roundtrip, and requires no local server to run. It claims design-system components and tokens can guide generated UI.
F_documentation.comparison_with_server_logic: OAuth challenge and metadata are directly observable. The public server implementation is unavailable, so most product claims and client recommendations cannot be compared with server-side enforcement. The repository contains client skills, not server handlers. Paid-plan and credit statements conflict across official pages.

contradictions: Official product page says users can “start building for free” and answers “Do I need a paid plan to start?” with “No”; the two official MCP setup guides say MCP integration requires a paid plan. https://www.magicpatterns.com/product/mcp ; https://www.magicpatterns.com/blog/aeo/blog/implementation-guide/set-up-the-magic-patterns-mcp-server-connect-your-coding-agent-to-your-design

The Claude connector directory and Manufact list three tools (get_design, read_files, update_design), while Scalekit lists 47 routed tools with different names. The vendor's public docs do not publish an exact product tool list, so this cannot be resolved from official tool definitions. https://claude.com/connectors/magic-patterns ; https://manufact.com/mcp-catalog/magic-patterns ; https://docs.scalekit.dev/agentkit/connectors/magicpatternsmcp/

The OAuth protected-resource metadata lists authorization-code, refresh-token, and device-code support in the authorization-server document, while the OIDC configuration additionally lists client_credentials. No corresponding MCP product behavior is documented. https://oauth.magicpatterns.com/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server ; https://oauth.magicpatterns.com/.well-known/openid-configuration
observations_for_research: The public plugin repository distributes agent skills that prescribe multi-step workflows; those client instructions may shape agent behavior independently of the hosted server's tool descriptions.

The MCP tool surface is represented inconsistently across third-party catalogues: three generic design tools versus 47 detailed routed operations, including file, canvas, shell-like, generation, and destructive operations.
Authentication metadata advertises generic identity scopes rather than product-specific design or write scopes; product-level authorization semantics remain undocumented.
notes: Checked the prepared links.json, links_check.txt, pages/ including pageN.script.txt files, and the local repository at commit 95423dbebeed508436bcedad8df39334f05b7f28. The repository is an official client-plugin and skills repo, not the hosted server code. The `/docs/mcp` page is a separate docs-search MCP manifest and was excluded from product actions. MCP.so has no displayed tool list; Manufact and Claude list three tools; Scalekit lists 47 routed operations. The official pricing page's collected copy was client-rendered and lacked readable prices, so pricing details use official product search results and the official pricing-change article. No detailed privacy policy text or hosted product tool schemas were found.
